title: v1/chat.completions: robust stop coalescing, role-alias translation, and framed tool-output batching
author: Nora Patel
description:
Motivation: Bring the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer closer to parity while improving streaming resilience for tool/function outputs and preserving per-token logprobs for stop demarcation. Several customers reported mismatches between framed JSON tool outputs and legacy clients that expect compact deltas; this PR introduces a backwards-compatible coalescing mode and a role-aliasing layer to reduce downstream mapping complexity.

What this PR does: Implements a three-part compatibility strategy: (1) stop coalescing modes (hard|soft|legacy) that determine how stop tokens are applied and how partial tokens are attributed to logprobs during streaming; (2) a role_aliases mapping in the v1 adapter so callers can provide aliases (e.g. assistant -> system-assistant) while the runtime maps them back to canonical roles for scoring and safety checks; (3) framed JSON chunk batching for tool/function outputs with optional compact-delta fallback for older clients. Also: adds thorough integration tests and updates the Python/TS SDK adapters.

Changes included (high level): - adapter: v1/chat_completions adapter param parsing and new "stop_coalesce_mode" flag - runtime: streaming coalescer that tracks token boundaries and retains token-level logprob attribution when stops are encountered mid-chunk - tool-output: framed JSON slice metadata (slice_id, seq, eof) and a compact_delta_fallback toggle - SDKs: Python and TypeScript wrappers expose new param mappings and provide automatic client-side fallback heuristics - docs: migration guide and examples for new flags and role_aliases mapping

Checklist: - [x] API adapter param mapping and validation - [x] Runtime coalescer + perf tests - [x] SDK bindings (python + ts) - [x] Integration tests for streaming + tool handoff - [x] Docs + migration guide - [x] Security review (audit of role alias resolution)

Commit summary: - add v1 stop_coalesce_mode parsing and validation - implement streaming coalescer with token-logprob tethering - add framed JSON slice envelope and compact-delta fallback - expose role_aliases mapping in v1 adapter and SDKs - add integration tests and test fixtures for fragmented tool outputs - docs: add openai compat migration / examples

Changed areas/files (representative): - src/api/v1/chat_completions_adapter.rs - runtime/streaming/coalescer.cpp - runtime/streaming/coalescer.h - sdk/python/redwood/openai_compat.py - sdk/typescript/src/openaiCompatAdapter.ts - docs/openai_compatibility/migration_chat_completions.md - tests/integration/test_chat_parity_stream.py - tests/fixtures/framed_tool_slices/*.json - .github/workflows/stream-integration.yml

Testing & QA: Ran unit tests and the integration stream harness locally and in CI. The integration/stream-harness showed a transient failure on the first run due to test timing; a rerun passed. Added a new e2e scenario that simulates a mid-chunk stop token and asserts that token-level logprobs are attributed to the prior token and that the framed JSON slices reconstruct correctly when reassembled. Performance impact: coalescer adds negligible CPU overhead in hot paths; added microbenchmarks to perf-canary.

Migration notes: - Default behavior remains legacy-compatible (stop_coalesce_mode=legacy). Administrators can enable soft or hard modes per-route to tighten stop enforcement or prefer minimal token chopping. - role_aliases is optional; when present the adapter will map incoming role names into canonical roles before applying safety checks. SDKs default to an empty mapping. - Framed JSON slices are opt-in via framed_output=true; the compact_delta_fallback=true flag enables older clients to continue receiving delta sequences as before.

Rollout plan: - Canary on dedicated capacity for 48h with canary workloads - Monitor token-level latency, stream reassembly success rate, and role-mapping anomalies - If metrics are stable, rollout to hosted API next week - Add migration note to release page and email major customers with instructions

Default behavior remains legacy-compatible. See migration guide in docs/openai_compatibility/migration_chat_completions.md.
